intended_object: The real part ℜ a = ½(a + a*) of an element a of a complex star module, viewed as an ℝ-linear map into the self-adjoint elements. The docstring says this and also explains why the definition exists.
explanation:
The body is `selfAdjointPart ℝ`. That map sends x to ⟨⅟2 • (x + star x), _⟩, which is exactly the standard real part ½(a + a*), as an ℝ-linear map into `selfAdjoint A`.

There is a more general construction: `selfAdjointPart R` works over any commutative semiring R with ⅟2 and a trivial star. But the docstring says outright that `realPart` is that map specialized to ℝ, with A a ℂ-module, so that it can be paired with `imaginaryPart`. The imaginary part a ↦ (a − a*)/(2i) only makes sense over ℂ, and so does the real/imaginary decomposition a = ℜa + i·ℑa. So the complex setting is the natural one for "real part", not an arbitrary restriction.

The hypotheses are the minimal ones needed: an additive commutative group that is a ℂ-module, with a star operation compatible with scalar multiplication. Since the body makes sense as defined, the definition is faithful.
